subject: Elastic allowance negotiation & overage mechanics — post-demo follow-up
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Cheng <natalie@finvoy.com>
Cc: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@finvoy.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Elastic allowance negotiation & overage mechanics — post-demo follow-up

Hi Natalie — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap + two asks so we can put together a tight pricing scenario for procurement: 

Recap:
- Use case: real-time credit decisioning + batch overnight embeddings for analytics. Typical request sizes: 256–1024 tokens per call for decisions; embeddings ~768 tokens per doc.
- Traffic pattern: baseline steady 1–2M tokens/day with periodic intra-day surges up to ~12M tokens in a couple of hours during market opens.
- Key constraint: procurement wants a predictable monthly cost but flexibility for surges during product launches.

Two asks (so we model unit economics accurately):
1) Can you confirm a target $/1M tokens range that feels reasonable for procurement? (ballpark is fine, we used $600–$1200 in the call)
2) What monthly token volumes should we model for the next 6 months? (min / typical / peak) — this helps decide whether Dedicated or Hosted with an elastic allowance is better.

Attached a quick worksheet we started (finvoy-maup-usage-estimate.xlsx) — fill in any numbers you want us to assume.

I'll loop Ben and Marissa on pricing scenarios once we get your ranges. We can propose: a) hosted with burst-credit allowance, b) hosted with higher quota and capped overage, or c) dedicated pool (if volumes justify).

Next steps: if you can send ranges and an internal procurement contact, we’ll return a 1-page commercial with explicit $/1M token scenarios and overage mechanics by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Natalie Cheng <natalie@finvoy.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@finvoy.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Elastic allowance negotiation & overage mechanics — post-demo follow-up

Connor — thanks, appreciated. Quick answers below so you can model: 

1) Budget: procurement gave a hard preference for predictability. They're comfortable with a committed run-rate that equates to ~$900/1M tokens as a mid-point. Upper bound they flagged is $1,300/1M if we get dedicated latency SLAs.

2) Volumes (monthly):
- Min: 20M tokens/month (slow month)
- Typical: 60M tokens/month
- Peak month (product launch): 220M tokens/month, usually concentrated in 48–72 hour windows with intra-day surges up to 12–15M tokens/hour for short bursts.

Procurement is asking specifically about:
- Burst / surge handling: can we define a short-term soft cap with automatic overage billing versus explicit quota increases?
- Overage caps: is there a way to cap monthly overage spend (e.g., auto-stop at +25% of committed spend) so they don't get surprised?
- Rate limits: what's the practical per-second request limit for hosted endpoints before we recommend dedicated pools?

I'll introduce Alex (procurement) if you want to route commercial language through them.

Thanks,
Natalie Cheng
VP of Product, FinVoy
Natalie.Cheng@finvoy.com

[Inline: pasted example traffic pattern from our SREs]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Cheng <natalie@finvoy.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Elastic allowance negotiation & overage mechanics — post-demo follow-up

Natalie — appreciate the numbers, that's very helpful. I put together three concise commercial scenarios and an overage mechanics summary. Attaching the one-pager (redwood-proposal-FV-v1.pdf). Key bullets below.

Scenario A — Hosted / Elastic Allowance (low commitment)\- Baseline commit: 60M tokens/month\- Included burst credit: 10M tokens/month pooled (resets monthly)\- Overage: $1,100 / 1M tokens on usage above commit + allowance\- Soft cap option: enable auto-stop at +25% over commit (procurement must opt in)\- Typical recommendation: good for firms testing product-market fit; predictable up to moderate surges.

Scenario B — Hosted / Higher Commit + Lower Overage\- Baseline commit: 100M tokens/month\- Included burst credit: 25M tokens/month\- Overage: $850 / 1M tokens\- If sustained peaks exceed 150M/mo, recommend moving to Dedicated.

Scenario C — Dedicated Pool (reserved capacity)\- Reserved baseline: 150M tokens/month equivalent\- Effective unit cost: $600 / 1M tokens (after reserved discount)\- Burst handling: configured autoscale + short-duration burst credits; sustained high traffic needs capacity add-ons\- SLA: 99.9% uptime SLA and tailored rate limits

Overage & Rate Limit mechanics (short):
- Burst allowance = temporary token credit applied at the account level; bursts consume credit first, then hit overage pricing.
- Soft cap behavior = system will pause request processing if monthly bill risk exceeds chosen threshold; we can alert + require manual override.
- Per-second rate recommendation = for hosted endpoints, keep sustained concurrency under 2.5k tokens/sec per model shard; for your peaks we recommend Dedicated if sustained > 5k tokens/sec for more than 30 minutes.

Attachment contains worked examples with your peak/typical numbers showing monthly cost, 95th percentile hourly rates, and a recommended path to Dedicated.

Next steps: Connor and I can turn the preferred scenario into a quote. If procurement wants an overage cap baked into contract we can outline contract language and a one-time committed top-up to cover initial burst window.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales 
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Elastic allowance negotiation & overage mechanics — post-demo follow-up

Ben / Connor — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs before I route to procurement: 

1) Burst allowance mechanics: does the allowance apply instantly to concurrent requests (i.e., no queuing) or do we see elevated latency as bursts consume credits?
2) Soft cap: if we enable auto-stop at +25%, can we also get a notification webhook to our billing channel and an emergency override endpoint? Procurement will want both.
3) If we opt for a temporary committed top-up to cover a launch (one-off), can that top-up be applied retroactively for a specific billing cycle to smooth the committed effective $/1M?

If those answers are positive we should be able to move quickly. Please call out any constraints on changing allowance mid-month.

Thanks,
Natalie

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Cheng <natalie@finvoy.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rajiv Malhotra <rajiv@finvoy.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Elastic allowance negotiation & overage mechanics — post-demo follow-up

Natalie — quick answers inline, and a proposed next-step plan so we keep momentum.

1) Burst allowance mechanics:
- Applies instantly at the account level; requests are not queued by default. The allowance is consumed first, and once exhausted requests fall back to overage pricing. We can optionally enable a short buffer queue (hundreds of ms) to smooth spikes but that adds a small latency tail.

2) Soft cap + notifications:
- Yes — we can enable auto-stop at a set overage threshold, provide webhook notifications to a billing Slack/email channel, and an authenticated override endpoint for emergency temporary lift. We’ll put guardrails on the override (time-limited + audit logs).

3) One-off committed top-up (retroactive application):
- Yes — we can apply a pre-paid top-up to a specific billing cycle if committed and invoiced before cycle close. That will lower effective $/1M for that cycle and can be used to partially offset overage.

Constraints:
- Changing allowance mid-month is supported, but we recommend changes take effect at the start of the next billing cycle for accounting simplicity. Immediate changes are possible but require approvals and may pro-rate included credits.

Proposed next steps (timeline):
- Today: Ben to send final 1-page price quote with the scenario you prefer (A/B/C) and explicit overage cap language for procurement review.
- Tomorrow: Draft contract addendum with a +25% soft cap clause and emergency override process if you want it in writing.
- This week: Sales Engineering trial (2 weeks) with a 10M token one-time burst credit to validate peak behavior; we’ll instrument latency/99th metrics and share dashboards.

If that works I’ll schedule a 30-min procurement walk-through with Alex and Rajiv for Thursday.
